questions.q: What does the Derived Column transformation do?
options: Creates new column values by applying expressions to input columns, variables, and functions
Sorts input rows by one or more columns
Loads a reference dataset into a memory cache for joining
Aggregates rows into groups with SUM, COUNT, and AVERAGE
questions.explain: The Derived Column transformation evaluates an expression — built from variables, functions, operators, and input columns — and writes the result as a new or replacement column value.

questions.q: What are the two placement choices for a derived column's result?
options: Add it as a new output column, or replace the value in an existing column
Send it to the Match output or the No Match output
Store it in full cache or partial cache
Write it to a raw file or a cache file
questions.explain: Every derived column can either become a brand-new column in the output, or overwrite the value of an existing input column — both run the same expression.

questions.q: If a Derived Column expression references a column that this same transformation is also configured to overwrite, what value does the expression see?
options: The original, pre-derived value of that column
The newly derived value, since it's evaluated first
A null value, since the column is mid-overwrite
It causes a circular reference error and the package fails to run
questions.explain: If an expression references an input column that the Derived Column transformation is overwriting, the expression uses the column's original value, not the value being derived.

questions.q: When you add a Derived Column result to a NEW output column, how are its data type, length, precision, and scale set?
options: The editor automatically evaluates the expression and sets them; the fields are read-only
You must manually type in every value with no automatic detection
They default to DT_STR with length 50 and can never be changed
They're inherited directly from the package's global variables
questions.explain: For a new column, the Derived Column Transformation Editor automatically evaluates the expression and sets data type, length, precision, and scale — you can only adjust the Code Page for string data.

questions.q: Which expression correctly matches Microsoft's own example for extracting a person's first initial from a FirstName column?
options: SUBSTRING(FirstName,1,1)
FirstName + "1"
ROUND(FirstName, 1)
DATEPART("year", FirstName)
questions.explain: SUBSTRING(FirstName,1,1) extracts the first character of the FirstName column — Microsoft's documented example for this exact use case.
